The Suborned · brief 056

Unity at full power

What Unity can do, what we use today, and the shortest path from the build we have to the 26 Sep paintings.

24 Oct 2026 · build 0.2.98 · from six crew studies (Vela, Glint, Redline, Latch, Splice, Pulse)

Where we are

The bones are right. The light and the life aren't there yet.

The layout, palette and camera already match. The gap is how light behaves, what moves, and how worn and lived-in things look.

2

How a Unity frame is made

Every frame runs the same chain, about 60 times a second

CullWork out what the camera can see.GPU Resident Drawer, LODs
›
ShadowsDraw the scene from the sun.4096 map, tactical fit
›
OpaqueDraw every solid surface and light it.Forward+, our shaders
›
Screen effectsSSAO, decals, reflections.SSAO only
›
Sky, glassSkybox, then see-through things.SubornedSky, glass film
›
PostGrade, tonemap, bloom.ACES grade volume
›
OverlaySignals, HUD.unlit signals, UI Toolkit

Pipeline: URP

The Universal Render Pipeline. You build the chain from parts: renderer features, volumes and shaders. Everything in this deck slots into one of those boxes.

The budget is per frame

60 fps means 16.7 ms for the whole chain on the 15-inch Air. Every look feature costs milliseconds somewhere in it. On the Air the GPU is the limit, not the CPU.

Already in the game

More than it looks like: the engine room is solid

URP 17.6, Forward+ GPU Resident Drawer SRP Batcher LOD groups Custom HLSL shaders: sky, facade, water, signals, crossing glow Shadows: 4096 map, fitted to the street Grade volume: ACES, bloom Day and night phase Input System UI Toolkit HUD Animator, LOD figures Streaming mipmaps (new, 0.2.98) Reflection probes: only 2 SSAO: on, but invisible at play zoom Render scale: plain upscale Light cookies: on, unused Night lamps: 28 Baked indirect light Anti-aliasing (play camera: none) Decals Particles Wind or sway Shader Graph Audio
usingpartlynot yet

The deterministic sim lives outside Unity (integer C#, 10 Hz). Unity only draws it, so every look feature here is safe for replays as long as nothing it computes flows back into the sim.

4

The gap, named

Six things the painting does that the game doesn't

1 2 3 4 5 6
  1. Glass with depth. Windows read as rooms and reflected sky. Ours are flat panels.
  2. Chrome that reflects. The globes and posts mirror the street. Ours reflect two probes.
  3. Soft bounce light. Warm light under canopies and in corners. Our shade is one flat value.
  4. Air and distance. The sea and far blocks fade into haze.
  5. Movement. Water sprays, palms and banners sway, people fill the square.
  6. Lived-in ground. Paving with wear, edges and dirt. Ours is clean tile.
5

Lever 1 · light

Adaptive Probe Volumes: light that bounces

What
Unity bakes a 3D grid of light samples once, at build time. At runtime every surface and every person reads the bounce light around it.
For us
Darker canyons and undersides of the deck and concourse. Warm cream-stone bounce on chrome and on the cell. Sky occlusion follows the live sky, so day and night still work, and Lighting Scenarios can blend between baked states.
Cost
Under 0.5 ms (Glint's estimate). Bake time is unknown. Civic block only.
Gap
3 · bounce
Verdict
proof once SSAO savings free the room
6

Lever 2 · chrome and glass

Reflections and fake interiors

proof

More reflection probes

Chrome is a house material, but it only has two probes to reflect. A probe per street or plaza, blended and box-projected (both already on), makes globes and posts mirror the street they stand in. Cost: memory, and almost no frame time.

proof

Interior-mapped windows

A shader trick: each window shows a fake room with depth, picked from a small atlas, with no geometry. Rooms you can't enter are a fit for "exteriors only". About 1 texture read per glass pixel. Sky's call on the look.

do

HDR grading, 64 LUT

The grade is LDR with a 32-step lookup today, and pastel cream gradients band first. Switching is free per frame, but every colour shifts a little, so Glint re-tunes it once.

Gaps 1 and 2. Screen-space reflections exist too, but they cost fill rate and soften chrome edges. Not for the Air.

7

Lever 3 · the ground

Decals: paint projected onto the world

What
A box that projects a texture onto whatever is inside it: road, paving, kerbs. No new geometry, no UV work.
For us
Wear and grime at kerbs and doors. Paint, drains and puddles. Bodies and Trail marks that stay where they fell ("live with it"). Target rings that sit under feet instead of over shoes (briefs 046 and 049).
Cost
Around 0.1 to 0.3 ms for a few dozen on screen. One renderer feature to add.
Note
The renderer is Forward+, so Unity uses its DBuffer decals, which also land on facades.
Verdict
proof one chalk mark, one body, one ring
8

Lever 4 · movement

A city that breathes

proof

Particle System

Fountain spray, steam vents, sparks from a looped camera, the Tech's loop. Small bursts of 20 to 200 particles, under 0.3 ms. Use the built-in Particle System, not VFX Graph.

proof

Shader wind

Palms, cypresses, banners and awnings sway in the vertex shader, driven by a global wind value. It costs almost nothing and reads at play zoom.

later

Animation Rigging

Heads that turn toward what a person sees. A witness looking at the body shows "who sees it" without any text, which is the "less reading" goal.

later

GPU crowds

Baked animation played on the GPU (vertex animation textures) for background people. Many more people per millisecond than Animators allow.

Gap 5. All of these only show the sim, seeded from plan ids. The sim decides who moves and where. Unity only adds the sway and the spray.

9

Lever 5 · air, edges, style

The finishing pass

do

Anti-aliasing

The play camera runs with none, so lamp posts, rails and kerbs stair-step. SMAA is a cheap fix. STP (next slide) fixes the edges and pays for itself.

proof

Haze and depth

Height fog and distance tint (atmospheric perspective) turn the sea and far towers soft, as in the painting. Screen-space lens flare and bloom on lamps fill the night. Gap 4.

later

A house style pass

A renderer feature can add a thin outline on people only, using rendering layers. That helps 40 to 60 px figures read. A soft painterly filter could pull the street toward the paintings. Shader Graph makes both quick to try.

Signals stay outside all of this. They are drawn unlit and emissive on their own overlay, so no grade, fog or bloom can change how they read.

10

Paying for it

The Air buys looks with GPU time. STP is the bank.

STP, in one line

Spatial-Temporal Post-processing renders at about 75% resolution, then rebuilds a sharp full-size frame from the last few frames. You get anti-aliasing and a large GPU saving in one feature. Built into Unity 6 URP.

The risk

Temporal methods can ghost on small moving things, which here means our 40 to 60 px people. It must be judged in play, not from stills.

All bars are estimates until the Air run. Today's estimate is Redline's (Studio GPU time × 4 to 4.5). The others add the study numbers to it.

11

What Unity offers that we skip

Powerful, but wrong for this game

NavMeshneverThe sim paths on its own integer grid. Mission timings depend on path length to 0.1 s, so replays would break.
TimelineneverCutscene tracks are hand-authored, and the rule is "nothing hand-authored". The fail camera is built per cause at runtime.
Occlusion cullingnoThe play view draws 325 objects. The cost is pixels, not objects. The GPU version made third person 36% slower.
VFX GraphnoBuilt for millions of particles. We need hundreds, and the Particle System does that more cheaply.
Burst and Jobsif neededFast multithreaded code, but the CPU isn't the bottleneck. It would save 0.2 to 0.4 ms at most.
CinemachinelaterWorth it only if third person returns. It would replace about 200 lines.
AddressableslaterAsset streaming. It earns its keep once there are two or three districts.
Lightmaps, realtime GInoAPV does the job for a generated world, and realtime GI is over the Air's budget.
12

Tools that make this faster

Seeing what the GPU sees

Frame Debugger

Steps through one frame draw by draw. It proves what SSAO, shadows and decals each add, and settles questions like "does SSAO even show?" in a minute.

Rendering Debugger

Shows lighting only, albedo only, overdraw, and the probe grid live in a build. It's how Glint tunes APV and reflections.

Profiler (GPU)

Real per-pass milliseconds on the Air instead of estimates. It plugs into the existing perf harness.

Shader Graph

Node-based shaders. Fast to try wind, interior windows and outlines before anyone hand-writes HLSL.

Unity Recorder

Records clean video from play or a replay for trailers, reviews and before-and-after comparisons.

Memory Profiler

Shows where the 855 MB goes at runtime, not only on disk.

13

Suggested path

Measure, save, then spend

Air run

Build 0.2.98 is waiting on the Air. About 2 minutes, plugged in. It turns every estimate here into a number.

Free the GPU

SSAO off for the play camera. STP or SMAA for clean edges. Cheaper shadows.

Light and chrome

APV over the civic block, a probe per street, HDR grade. Shown to you as before and after.

Life and wear

Decals, shader wind, a few particle effects.

Style

Interior windows, haze, people outlines. Judged against the paintings.

Capstone friction still comes first. Steps 1 and 2 serve the 60 fps limit. Steps 3 to 5 are listed in briefs/parked.md until you pick them up. Every step is one batch and one rebuild.
